name: Dimethandrolone undecanoate

lead: Dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) is an experimental oral drug that acts as both an androgen and a progestin. It is being developed mainly as a male contraceptive pill and secondarily for androgen replacement, and forum users speculate it could work as an oral anabolic for muscle.

After ingestion the ester is cleaved to dimethandrolone, which activates androgen and progesterone receptors and is not converted to estrogen by aromatase in laboratory tests. In men it suppresses LH, FSH, testosterone and estradiol. Human trials so far are short studies in healthy men looking at safety, pharmacokinetics and hormone suppression; none has tested muscle or appearance.

paras: It is not available as a medicine; research use has been as a once-daily oral in clinical trials. In forums it appears mostly as a news item about male contraception or as a hypothetical oral anabolic.

Not approved anywhere. Short trials report hormone suppression, effects on bone turnover markers and metabolic changes; long-term safety is not established. Hormonal male contraceptives as a class face problems with side effects and non-response.

angle.text: Forum users speculate that DMAU could become an oral anabolic, since it is a potent androgen that works by mouth and could add muscle mass. It was developed as a male contraceptive pill; trials looked at hormone levels and safety rather than muscle or looks.

lead: Dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) is an experimental, orally active synthetic androgen with progestational activity. It is an ester prodrug: enzymes in the body cleave off the undecanoate group to release the active compound, dimethandrolone (7alpha,11beta-dimethyl-19-nortestosterone), a 19-nortestosterone derivative [1][2]. It has been developed mainly as a candidate male hormonal contraceptive and, secondarily, as a possible androgen replacement therapy [3][4][2].

For people interested in appearance, the interest is in the androgen side of the drug: androgens such as testosterone drive muscle, facial and body hair, jaw and bone development, and DMAU is a non-aromatizing androgen that does not need 5alpha-reduction for its effects, so forum users have wondered about it as an oral anabolic. That is a hypothetical chain; the research programme has been built around contraception, and no human study has tested muscle, body composition or other appearance outcomes [5][6][7].

DMAU is not approved anywhere for any use. Published human work consists of early-phase trials in healthy men examining safety, pharmacokinetics and suppression of testosterone and gonadotropins [5][6]. It was developed by the Contraceptive Development Branch of the US National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, and results of its 28-day trial in 2018 drew coverage from outlets including NBC News and the Chicago Tribune, according to Wikipedia's reference list [2]. In bodybuilding and anabolic steroid forums it appears mostly as a news item about male contraception or as a hypothetical oral anabolic [8][9].
infobox: Dimethandrolone patent filed 1997; DMAU patent filed 2002, granted 2003 [2]

paras: DMAU has been developed as a once-daily oral male contraceptive prototype. Reviews describe it as one of several single-agent hormonal candidates, alongside 11beta-methyl-nortestosterone dodecylcarbonate and 7alpha-methyl-19-nortestosterone, with the aim of suppressing luteinizing hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone and testosterone to reduce sperm production [3][4][10]. Its androgenic activity is intended to maintain male-typical hormone effects while the progestin-like activity helps suppress gonadotropins [1][11].

No human study has examined DMAU for muscle growth, fat loss or other cosmetic outcomes. Animal work in castrated rats measured body composition, bone mineral density and androgenic and anabolic activity over longer periods [12], but this is not a test of use in healthy men. Forum users on T Nation have discussed it as a possible oral anabolic steroid, with several noting that its research focus is contraception rather than performance [13][14].

DMAU is a synthetic estrane steroid and a non-17alpha-alkylated derivative of 19-nortestosterone. It is the 17beta-undecanoate (undecylate) ester of dimethandrolone, which carries methyl groups at the 7alpha and 11beta positions. Related esters from the same programme include dimethandrolone buciclate and dimethandrolone dodecylcarbonate; the NICHD programme also developed the related compound 11beta-methyl-19-nortestosterone dodecylcarbonate (11beta-MNTDC), which has been compared with DMAU in men.[2][15]

In laboratory characterisation, DMAU was orally active in castrate rat bioassays and showed both androgen-receptor and progestin-receptor activity after the ester was cleaved to dimethandrolone [1]. Work with recombinant human aromatase found that dimethandrolone and a related compound were not converted to aromatic A-ring (estrogen-like) products, meaning it is described as non-aromatizable [16]. A further study found that dimethandrolone did not require 5alpha-reduction to exert its maximal androgenic effects [7].
In men, the combination of androgenic and progestational action suppresses LH and FSH, lowering the body's own testosterone and estradiol output [5][6].

Wikipedia notes that dimethandrolone is not a substrate for 5alpha-reductase, and describes this as a reason it may carry fewer of the androgenic effects associated with testosterone's conversion, such as acne, scalp hair loss and prostate effects; this has not been tested against testosterone in head-to-head human trials.[2][7]

Early single-dose studies in men examined absorption, food effects and formulation differences, reporting that the oral drug was tolerated and that serum levels and hormone suppression depended on the formulation and on food intake [11][17]. An analytical paper also noted that measuring androgen esters in blood is complicated by ex vivo esterase activity and assay interference [18].

Wikipedia reports that in a study of men given DMAU powder in capsules only about 2 to 3 percent was converted to dimethandrolone, attributed by the authors to steric hindrance from the methyl groups, and that conversion improved when the drug was delivered in oil-based or self-emulsifying formulations.[2]

A phase 1 single-dose escalation trial in men studied pharmacokinetics, safety and food effects of oral DMAU as a prototype male hormonal contraceptive [17], and a randomized comparison tested two oral formulations in single doses [11]. A registered phase 1 trial enrolled 100 healthy men [19].

In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 100 healthy men aged 18 to 50 received oral DMAU or placebo for 28 days. The investigators assessed safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, and the study is described as a prototype male pill [5]. A companion analysis of 81 men receiving 0, 100, 200 or 400 mg for 28 days found marked suppression of serum testosterone and estradiol compared with placebo, and a difference between groups in the bone formation marker P1NP, with increases in some dose groups. The authors were interested in whether estradiol suppression would affect bone turnover [6]. A survey of 57 trial participants examined their satisfaction with and acceptability of the daily regimen [20]. A randomized comparison of DMAU and 11beta-MNTDC also examined metabolic effects in healthy men [15].

Wikipedia's summary of the 2018 one-month study states that daily oral dosing suppressed testosterone to levels (about 13.4 ng/dL on average) close to those after surgical castration (about 15 ng/dL), that testosterone recovered within days of stopping and normalised within a month, and that the drug was well tolerated with mild weight gain and small decreases in HDL cholesterol reported. It adds that actual contraceptive effectiveness and sperm suppression had not yet been tested at that point.[2][5]

An injectable DMAU phase 1 trial (n=106) and a phase 2 trial of spermatogenesis suppression with DMAU alone or with levonorgestrel versus placebo (n=92) are registered as completed [21][22]. Reviews note that, as of mid-2023, DMAU was in trials focusing on safety, pharmacodynamics and suppression of spermatogenesis and hormones [10]. These studies were not designed to measure physique, and no outcome relevant to appearance has been reported. Longer-term effects have not been established in published trials.

Safety data come from short trials in healthy volunteers. The 28-day trials looked at effects on hormones, bone turnover markers and metabolic parameters [5][6][15]. Because DMAU suppresses estradiol as well as testosterone, researchers have specifically examined bone markers, since estradiol deficiency can increase bone resorption in men [6]. Rabbit research examined effects of synthetic androgens on liver function as a model [23]. Reviews of male hormonal contraception generally list adverse effects, injection or implant requirements and a 5 to 10 percent non-response rate as hurdles for hormonal methods as a class [3][24]. Long-term safety in humans has not been established.

Wikipedia notes that because DMAU suppresses testosterone and therefore estrogen, symptoms of low estrogen such as reduced libido, erectile dysfunction and bone loss may occur, as with the related compound trestolone, and that animal studies showed some signs of possible liver effects, far smaller than with methyltestosterone, while the clinical study found liver and kidney function acceptable over one month.[2][23]

Dimethandrolone undecanoate was described in 2006 in the journal Endocrinology as a potent, orally active androgen with progestational activity under development for therapeutic uses in men [1]. Subsequent preclinical papers examined its resistance to aromatization and 5alpha-reduction and its long-term effects in castrated male rats [12][16][7]. Reviews state that pharmaceutical development of male contraception was largely dormant after the 1990s, and that the NICHD, which has supported contraceptive development since 1969, funds most ongoing hormonal male contraceptive work including DMAU [4][4]. Phase 1 trials began in 2012, and phase 2 in 2018 [19][22].

According to Wikipedia, a patent on dimethandrolone was filed in 1997 and granted in 1999, and a patent covering DMAU and dimethandrolone buciclate was filed in 2002 and granted to the US government in 2003. The first clinical studies in men were single-dose studies published in 2014 and 2015, followed by the 28-day study in 2018.[2][17][5]
DMAU is an investigational drug and is not marketed or approved for prescription. Its use outside trials is not authorised.

A 2018 T Nation post described the 28-day study as making headlines, summarising the drug as lowering testosterone to pre-pubertal levels [8]. Forum discussions refer to it in debates on male birth control and in lists of oral androgens, with some users speculating about its suitability as an anabolic steroid while others point out that research has been directed at contraception [13][14][25].

The 2018 trial results were covered by the Endocrine Society, Live Science, MedPage Today, NBC News and the Chicago Tribune, according to the reference list of Wikipedia's article, which is how many forum users first heard of the drug.[2]
